title: PatientLevelPrediction with Strategus
text:
1 Overview
This document shows how to:

Load cohort JSONs and generate cohorts using CohortGenerator.
Configure a PatientLevelPrediction (PLP) design.
Assemble Strategus analysis specifications
Execute the analysis specifications against a DuckDB Synthea example database.

This is the tutorial reference. To run the tutorial we recommend using the R file which can be downloaded along with the cohorts in a zip file from here. This file contains the same code but is easier to run and modify step-by-step. Please start a new R project and extract the contents of the zip file into the project folder.


2 Setup
First we need to set up our environment.






TipPrerequisites




If you don’t have R installed please follow the HADES installation instructions for your operating system from here.
Usually to run OHDSI packages you need to install at least R, java and a github account (to install packages from github without rate-limiting).
Once you have that set up you can install the required packages for this tutorial. They are PatientLevelPrediction, CohortGenerator, CirceR, and Strategus.
Also to use the example database you need to install duckdb. Since Strategus is still under development you need to install it from github which requires the remotes package.
Further for viewing the results you will need OHDSIShinyAppBuilder and OhdsiShinyModules the latter is available on github.









NoteExample Data



Please download the example database from here and place in your location of choice. Then update the dbPath variable to point to that location. Note that the database is just over 4GB so it may take a while to download. During the tutorial it will be available from a usb stick.




Code
# Install required packages (uncomment if needed):
# install.packages(c("PatientLevelPrediction", "CohortGenerator", "CirceR", "remotes", "duckdb", "OHDSIShinyAppBuilder"))
# remotes::install_github("OHDSI/Strategus")
# remotes::install_github("OHDSI/OhdsiShinyModules"))

library(PatientLevelPrediction)
library(Strategus)

seed <- 42




Code
# this should point to your downloaded duckdb file
dbPath <- "~/database/database-1M_filtered.duckdb"




Code
# Database schemas and cohort table for our example database, if running against a different database these would need to be updated. CDM schema is where the OMOP CDM data is stored, work schema is where cohorts will be generated and cohort table is the name of the table to hold the cohorts in the cohortSchema. You need to have write access to the workSchema.
cdmSchema <- "main"
workSchema <- "cohorts"
cohortTable <- "cohort_table"




3 Cohort Generation
To generate the cohorts we need to load the JSON files and create a cohort definition set. Then we can create the shared resource specifications and module specifications for cohort generation.






NoteCohort JSONs




Download the JSON files from here.
Open each file and press download.
Save them somewhere locally and update the paths below to point to the location where you saved them.





Code
# These should point to your downloaded cohort JSON files. If you unzipped the tutorial files in the project folder you can use the paths as they are.
1targetFile <- "./cohorts/31_[T] Pandemic Prediction new target.json"
outcomeFile <- "./cohorts/14_[O] Pandemic Prediction outcome pneumonia in hospital.json"

2cohortDefinitions <- CohortGenerator::createEmptyCohortDefinitionSet()
cohortDefinitions[1, ] <- list(
  cohortId = 1,
  cohortName = "Target",
  sql = "",
  json = readChar(targetFile, file.info(targetFile)$size)
)
cohortDefinitions[2, ] <- list(
  cohortId = 2,
  cohortName = "Outcome",
  sql = "empty",
  json = readChar(outcomeFile, file.info(outcomeFile)$size)
)

3cohortGeneratorModule <- CohortGeneratorModule$new()
cohortDefShared <- cohortGeneratorModule$createCohortSharedResourceSpecifications(cohortDefinitions)

cohortGeneratorModuleSpecifications <- cohortGeneratorModule$createModuleSpecifications(
  generateStats = TRUE
4)



1

Point Strategus at the target and outcome cohort JSON files.

2

Load the cohort definitions into a Strategus-ready set.

3

Create shared resources so other modules can reuse the cohorts.

4

Create the cohort generation module specifications.






4 PLP Design
This section configures the PLP design by defining covariates, population settings, preprocessing, data splits, and the baseline model choice.






TipModel Variations




Use the baseline setLassoLogisticRegression call to reproduce the tutorial results.
Swap to the alternative model options listed in the code comments when you are ready to experiment.





Code
1covariateSettings <- FeatureExtraction::createDefaultCovariateSettings()

populationSettings <- createStudyPopulationSettings(
  binary = TRUE,
  removeSubjectsWithPriorOutcome = TRUE,
  requireTimeAtRisk = FALSE,
  riskWindowStart = 1,
  riskWindowEnd = 30,
2)

preprocessSettings <- createPreprocessSettings(
  minFraction = 0.001,
  normalize = TRUE,
  removeRedundancy = TRUE
3)

4splitSettings <- createDefaultSplitSetting(splitSeed = seed)

# Choose model based on parameter (baseline: lasso logistic)
5modelSettings <- PatientLevelPrediction::setLassoLogisticRegression(seed = seed)
  # Other options (require additional packages; see Exercises below):
  # PatientLevelPrediction::setGradientBoostingMachine(ntrees = 100, seed = seed),
  # PatientLevelPrediction::setRandomForest(ntrees = 100, seed = seed),

message(sprintf("Model selected: %s | Split seed: %s", "LASSO", seed))

modelDesign <- PatientLevelPrediction::createModelDesign(
  targetId = 1,
  outcomeId = 2,
  populationSettings = populationSettings,
  covariateSettings = covariateSettings,
  preprocessSettings = preprocessSettings,
  modelSettings = modelSettings,
  splitSettings = splitSettings,
  runCovariateSummary = TRUE
6)

plpModule <- PatientLevelPredictionModule$new()
7plpModuleSpecs <- plpModule$createModuleSpecifications(modelDesignList = modelDesign)



1

Generate a broad set of default covariates using FeatureExtraction.

2

Define cohort eligibility and the time-at-risk window.

3

Configure preprocessing to normalize features and drop redundancy.

4

Fix the train/test split seed for reproducibility.

5

Choose the baseline LASSO logistic regression model (swap here to explore alternatives).

6

Assemble the pieces into a complete model design.

7

Wrap the design in a PLP module specification Strategus can execute.






5 Strategus Analysis Specifications
With the cohort and PLP modules ready, assemble the Strategus analysis specifications and persist them for execution.






NoteOutput Artifact




analysisSpecifications.json captures the combined resources and module settings needed for execution. When executing a network study this file is shared with othes sites to execute the study.





Code
1analysisSpecifications <- createEmptyAnalysisSpecifications() |>
2  addSharedResources(cohortDefShared) |>
3  addModuleSpecifications(cohortGeneratorModuleSpecifications) |>
  addModuleSpecifications(plpModuleSpecs)

4ParallelLogger::saveSettingsToJson(analysisSpecifications, "analysisSpecifications.json")



1

Start from an empty Strategus analysis scaffold.

2

Attach the shared cohort definitions required downstream.

3

Include the cohort generator and PLP modules in the execution plan.

4

Persist the resulting specification to JSON for reuse or sharing.






6 Execution settings and running
Create the execution settings, point Strategus to your DuckDB database, and then run the analysis.






WarningBefore You Run




Confirm the work and results directories exist or can be created by Strategus.
Make sure the DuckDB file path is correct and accessible.
Expect execution to take a few minutes depending on data size.





Code
# Define where Strategus should store intermediate work files and final results
1workFolder <- "./results/strategus/work"
resultsFolder <- "./results/strategus/results"

executionSettings <- Strategus::createCdmExecutionSettings(
  workDatabaseSchema = workSchema,
  cdmDatabaseSchema = cdmSchema,
  cohortTableNames = CohortGenerator::getCohortTableNames(cohortTable = cohortTable),
  workFolder = workFolder,
  resultsFolder = resultsFolder,
  incremental = FALSE
2)

connectionDetails <- DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(
  dbms = "duckdb",
  server = dbPath
3)

# Execute the study (may take some minutes depending on data size)
Strategus::execute(
  analysisSpecifications,
  executionSettings = executionSettings,
  connectionDetails = connectionDetails
4)



1

Define where Strategus should store intermediate work files and final results.

2

Build execution settings that contain schemas, cohort tables, and output locations.

3

Supply connectionDetails for Strategus to reach your database.

4

Kick off the Strategus pipeline with the assembled specifications.

7 View Results






NoteInteractive Review





Use the PLP viewer to inspect the results produced by the execution step. Execute these lines when you are ready to launch the shiny viewer.


Code
analysisLocation <- file.path(workFolder, "PatientLevelPredictionModule")
PatientLevelPrediction::viewMultiplePlp(analysisLocation)







8 Exercises






TipReset Between Runs



If you plan to re-run the exercises with different settings, remove the contents of ./results/strategus/work/PatientLevelPredictionModule/ between runs so PLP does not skip running. Adjust the path if you used a different workFolder.



Explore Coefficients and Top Predictors: After running the analysis, use the PLP viewer to inspect the model coefficients and top predictors. How do these align with your expectations?
Model Exploration: Modify the modelSettings in the PLP design section to experiment with different algorithms like Random Forest (setRandomForest) or XGBoost (setGradientBoostingMachine). Make sure to choose a subset of hyperparameters so it doesn’t run forever. Observe how these changes impact model performance metrics.

Pay attention to how more flexible models influence training versus test performance and whether additional tuning is required.
Seed Variation: Change the seed variable to different values and rerun the analysis. Document how the results vary with different seeds, particularly focusing on model stability and performance consistency. What do you think is affecting the variablitiy in our case?
Network study: Share your analysisSpecifications.json file with a colleague and have them run your analysis.
Go Deep: Try to develop a deep learning model using setDefaultResNet from the DeepPatientLevelPrediction package. Install it first with install("DeepPatientLevelPrediction"). Note either on install or first run it will take a few minutes to set up the python dependencies.




Environment setup for extra models
# XGBoost
install.packages("xgboost")
# Random Forest via reticulate
install.packages("reticulate")
reticulate::py_require("scikit-learn")
